gaps.title: Non-autoregressive machine translation lags on long outputs
gaps.description: Reported speedups largely vanish for long outputs, where the number of refinement passes needed grows with the target length.

ideas.title: Entropy-Allocated Refinement: spend passes where the model is uncertain
ideas.description: A non-autoregressive decoder that allocates refinement passes by predictive entropy rather than by position or schedule. Positions are ranked by entropy after the first pass and only the top quantile is re-predicted, so compute concentrates on the hard, clustered positions (rare vocabulary, named entities) instead of being spread uniformly. The decoder stops when the entropy mass below the threshold falls under a tolerance, which makes the step count data-dependent rather than fixed.
ideas.one_liner: Allocate refinement compute by predictive entropy, not by length or schedule.

user_input.title: Merge request
user_input.text: These two are the same paper. Merge them: keep the confidence gating from the first and the entropy-based allocation from the second. Where they disagree — length-aware budget versus entropy-driven stopping — I want the conflict written down, not smoothed over.

conflicts.text: Idea A derives the pass budget from predicted output length before decoding starts. Idea B derives the stopping point from the entropy mass observed during decoding. One is an a-priori budget, the other an online stopping rule; they cannot both be the mechanism.

A freezes positions by a fixed confidence threshold tau; B re-predicts a top quantile of positions by entropy. A fixed threshold and a fixed quantile behave differently when the whole sequence is easy.
